Why Our School Should Start a Community Garden

I believe our school should start a community garden behind the gym. In my opinion, a garden would teach us more about science than any textbook could. When I visited my aunt's farm last summer, I learned how soil, water and sunlight work together to grow food. We could learn the same lessons right here at school.

First, a garden gives students hands-on science practice. My classmates and I could measure plant growth, test different soils and keep records over the year. Composting is the process of turning food scraps into rich soil. Our cafeteria throws away a lot of food scraps every day, and we could use them for compost instead.

Second, a garden would bring our community together. Families could volunteer on weekends, and older students could teach younger ones. I think working side by side would help us get to know each other better.

Some people worry that a garden would cost too much money. However, many seeds are cheap, and local stores often donate tools. I am confident that our school can raise the small amount needed with a bake sale.

In conclusion, a community garden would help us learn, bring families together and make our school a greener place. I hope the principal will agree that we should start one this spring.
